chapter: His own groups, compositions and friends
title: Recordings of his chamber works and Roots II
summary: Starker and Anne Akiko Meyers recorded his sonatas, and the piano trio Roots II for the Beaux Arts Trio is his best-known work.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: remember [Milos Jahoda] – somebody who’s from the London Symphony Orchestra [the Czech National Symphony Orchestra]. It was recorded with the National Czech Orchestra [the Czech National Symphony Orchestra] and it’s going to be out very soon. There’s also a recording of the Blues on an album called American Diversions by Jenny Spanoghe, who’s, I guess, French or Belgian?

Yes. There are any number of chamber works. There’s a piece – probably the best-known work is a piece called Roots II, which was written for the Beaux Arts Trio. It’s had probably 50 or 60 performances.
All over the world. That’s really . . .
. . . a piece that’s gotten a lot of . . .

And there are a couple of other piano trios: the one that I wrote for the Western Arts Trio, which is called Contrasts. There’s a number of string quartets: one called Through the Prism of the Black Experience, which is on an album called Through the Prism of the Black Experience. There’s a piece for jazz violin and string quartet. I don’t remember what I call it, but it is a piece for jazz violin and string quartet [Sonata for Jazz Violin and String Quartet].
